correctness.rationale: Folded angular differences are independent uniform on [0,π]. The squared ratio is a positive weighted average of the squared one-circle arc/chord factors, which increase strictly to (π/2)². It tends to 1 at the all-zero corner and reaches π/2 exactly on the other 2^d−1 corners, so all sufficiently high exceedances are localized there. Expanding at antipodal set A gives deficit F=L+O(L²) with L=Σ_{j∈A}r_j²s_j/(2S_A)+Σ_{i∉A}(π²−4)r_i²y_i²/(16πS_A); all coefficients are positive at fixed radii. In a small fixed neighborhood, F<ε is thus squeezed by L<ε±O(ε²). The volumes of these model sets scale exactly with exponent (d+|A|)/2. The squared-coordinate substitution and beta integral give c_A as stated, with a relative O(ε) error, so a singleton's next error cannot contribute to the second coefficient (including d=2). The AM–GM equality case is exactly equal radii. On singleton corners, rescaled model contributions have simplex density proportional to the product of inverse square roots of the coincident-coordinate contributions; adding slack gives Dirichlet(1,1/2,…,1/2,1). The squeeze implies the same law for the true exceedance and either exact or leading slack. Singleton corner weights are proportional to r_j^d, and the labelled ratios plus diameter determine the scale. All claims are for fixed positive radii and the specified embedding.

For radii (1,1), (1,2), (1.3,0.8), the residual after subtracting C_1 ε^(3/2), divided by ε², approaches the computed C_2, and the error after both terms divided by ε^(5/2) stays bounded across ε=0.003 to 0.0001. This is a finite diagnostic, not proof for all d. Frozen checks/verify_clifford_tail.py inspected, not executed.
